snippet.title: Everything We Know About the Final Season of Stranger Things

Matt and Ross Duffer have always known how the series will end and they’ve never deviated from that in any season. At the end of season four, we saw Max in pretty rough shape – even Sadie Sink isn’t sure what her fate is going to be, but we know that she is in an irreversible coma and that plays a huge part in the plot. We also can’t look to Millie Bobby Brown for any information because they don’t tell her anything – apparently, she has a huge mouth. In the upcoming season, we finally get to find out everything about Will and his connection to Vecna and the Upside Down. Remember when we found out that the Upside Down is stuck in 1983? The day Will went missing? We finally get answers to all of these burning questions. Season five is also not going to be without huge repercussions from the demise of Eddie Munson – we’re not sure how, but Matt and Ross Duffer have definitely confirmed that fact. Also, there’s going to be an invasion from the Upside Down into Hawkins, Indiana. There’s a lot more to unpack here, so make sure you stick around to the very end!

snippet.title: Actors Who Almost Quit the Business
snippet.description:
Whether or not you’re just an actor working to get into Hollywood - you know how hard it is to get there. But sometimes we forget that those celebs we all know and love - had experienced a ton of rejection! With this list of actors who made it - every single one of them quit at some point on their way to the top - and some quit a lot more than others.
There are so many reasons to quit a life of acting - one being rejection - which let’s be honest - an actor would have to embrace in order to get where they want to be. Another reason - which Robert Pattinson experienced so gracefully - is a horrible auditioning experience. Which he got anyways so luckily he salvaged that one. But not all of these actors experienced doubt in their careers at a later age - some felt the blunt end of the industry as a child actor. Adults have better times handling rejection - but for a kid? That’s extremely hard to let go of. Whether or not you're a child or adult actor - you will always need someone to give you that little pep talk to keep going. Even if it’s just the smallest push - it still changed the lives of these blockbuster stars.
We hope this video can inspire some you artists out there - and maybe even help make a Hollywood career seem more attainable. Because trust us - if Henry Cavill can have a career after his big audition flop - so can you!

snippet.title: The Real Story Behind Wednesday's Dance Scene
snippet.description:
Netflix’s Wednesday has everyone diving deep into the world of Wednesday Addams, portrayed by the incredible Jenna Ortega. In this video we’ll be digging deep into her iconic dance at the Rave’N. Did you know that Jenna Ortega actually choreographed the entire thing herself two days before the shoot? She didn’t have time to work on it that week because she was busy learning German, taking Cello lessons, and fencing! She really had her hands full. Tim Burton refused to work with a choreographer, so Jenna decided to take the task on herself. She ended up kicking herself down the line because she would not consider herself a dancer, much less a choreographer, and has never done anything like this before. Something else that’s pretty insane is the fact that she had Covid during the shoot! She woke up that day with some major body aches and an awful sore throat, but she didn’t end up getting the test results back until later, so she ended up having to shoot the scene in that condition. She even asked to redo it when she felt better, but they just didn’t have the time. We wonder how different the scene actually would’ve been. She uses a lot of artists and musicians as inspiration for her movies – even the OG Wednesday, Christina Ricci. Did you notice the original Wednesday Addams dance movie, The Drew? We’ll be getting into all of this, and much more!

Emma Myers was forced to attend what she referred to as ‘werewolf boot camp’ for her role as Wednesday Addams’ werewolf roommate Enid, which she remembered as being ‘weird.’ Tim Burton insisted on bringing in a real actor to portray Thing, similar to what director Barry Sonnenfeld had done for 1991’s The Addams Family and 1993’s The Addams Family Values. And so, magician Victor Dorobantu was brought in, wearing a full VFX suit! Brett Chan served as the stunt co-ordinator, and he’s worked on a number of incredibly impressive projects in the past. He has worked with Netflix previously on Marco Polo and Warrior, but he has also lended his skills in the world of movies with The Twilight Saga: Eclipse. Are you excited to get all of Wednesday’s hidden secrets about how Thing was created? In Netflix’s hit show, Wednesday, Victor Dorabantu plays the role of Wednesday Addams’ severed companion, Thing. Did you know that this was Victor’s first acting gig? He’s a magician by trade! Back in the 90s, Christopher Hart – who is also a magician – played the iconic role! The reason why they wanted to get magicians to audition for the part was due to the look of their hands as well as how nimble they were. It makes sense given how much Thing walks around the set and gets into things he shouldn’t. There were also some major difficulties and set backs when creating the character. For instance, Victor’s body had to be camouflaged as much as possible, because painting out the majority of his body was not an easy task for the special effects team. Often times they would put him under beds, behind Jenna Ortega, or even awkwardly around corners. It was important that the actor who played Thing was young and nimble enough to fit into this strange positions all the time. Victor also spent hours in make up getting his hand quaffed to perfection – we’ve got some incredible behind the scenes footage that shows his transformation into Thing. You wouldn’t think he would need so long in make up, but with how much detail goes into making his hand look the way we see on screen, there are a lot of details that could be easily overlooked.

snippet.title: Behind the Making of 1899
snippet.description:
Think you know what went into the making of 1899? Today, we’re going behind the scenes on Netflix’s newest series from showrunners Baron Bo Odar and Jantje Friese, the co-creators of Dark. It uses LED-Volume Technology completely unlike anything that we’ve ever seen come out of Netflix before! This technology uses a video game engine to build virtual sets, projecting the image onto what’s essentially a giant television set behind our actors. In fact, this new technology may just have been too good, considering Andreas Pietschmann actually got seasick on set! Far from being an excuse to make another costume drama history series, the showrunners actually put a lot of thought into their reasons for setting 1899 in the year they did. In fact, the showrunners even took care to include plenty of easter eggs sprinkled throughout the series to suggest that our characters may just be trapped in a simulation. Bad news for Keanu Reeves fans, but the opening credit song, “White Rabbit” by Jefferson Airplane, isn’t actually meant as a reference to the Matrix. That being said, there is a number of cinematic influences for 1899. Baron Bo Odar has said that he took inspiration from Ridley Scott’s Alien, and from Stanley Kubrick’s The Shining, but he wanted to go out of his way to avoid comparisons to James Cameron’s Titanic as much as possible! 1899 was filmed out of Potsdam, Germany, a city that actually is no stranger to Hollywood productions. Previous movies to have been filmed out of Potsdam include V For Vendetta, The Matrix Resurrections, and Inglourious Basterds.

snippet.description:
We know actors are insanely good at lying – it’s part of the job, but did you know that most of them actually had to lie to book the roles we couldn’t imagine anyone else playing? Sadie Sink was originally turned down for the role of Max because they thought she was too old – she was only fourteen at the time, so she didn’t want anything else going against her chances. So, when they asked her if she could rollerblade – the wanted someone who could skateboard to play Max – she said of course! Though she really had no confidence in her ability to skateboard or even rollerblade. She ended up having to learn in a month. Did you know Phoebe Dynevor lied about her ability to horseback ride to land her role in Bridgerton? Not only did she say she rode horses all the time and was super skilled at it, but she was also actually terrified of horses! She ended up loving the activity after taking horseback riding lessons with her costar. Robert Pattinson also lied to land the role of Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter! He lied about going to Oxford because he had been unemployed for so long he figured that was the best way to fill in that resume gap! He claims that when you’re British, that’s an easy thing to lie about. Who knew?! This list is full of actors who have told a white lie or two to land a role – you’d be surprised how common it is!

snippet.title: Behind the Making of Bones and All
snippet.description:
We’re taking a look at everything that went into the making of Bones and All! This film reunites Timothée Chalamet with the director of Call Me By Your Name, Luca Guadagnino. In fact, many of the talent working behind the scenes also worked with Luca Guadagnino in the past. Writer David Kajganich and costume designer Guilia Piersanti both worked on Call Me By Your Name, while actress Chloë Sevigny has worked with Luca Guadagnino on the HBO miniseries We Are Who We Are. This is Luca Guadagnino’s first time filming in the United States, and he’s spoken about how the setting of Ronald Reagan’s America had a huge influence on the film’s tone. The 1980’s have been a pretty popular setting in the media again this year, with 2022 already seeing the return of Stranger Things for Season Four. Meanwhile, Taylor Russell told Buzzfeed that some of the filming locations for Bones and All were haunted! And if battling ghosts on set weren’t enough, our cast also had to suffer some pretty disgusting meals. How would you enjoy eating platinum pure silicon drenched in syrup and brownies? Peter Saville, who has created the covers of albums for bands such as New Order and Joy Division, did all of the graphic design for Bones and All. Antonio Campos, who directed The Devil All The Time for Netflix, almost served as director for Bones and All when the film was still in early production, but when he backed out David Kajganich was able to convince Luca Guadagnino to take his place.

snippet.title: Behind the Magic of Disney's Strange World
snippet.description:
We’re diving into one of our all-time favorite topics – Disney movies! In Strange World, we’ve got incredible stars behind these characters. We’ve got Jake Gyllenhaal as Searcher, Gabrielle Union as Meridian and Lucy Liu as Callisto Mal. These three are such incredible, hard-working, seasoned performers that it’s kind of a no-brainer that there would be a lot of improv in the booth as well as collaboration on the film itself. Jake Gyllenhaal said when he first signed on, he only wanted to be involved if he could be very, very involved. He was extremely dedicated to his character and would often go back to the writers and have notes about the script. They would always re-write it for him based on what he thought his character truly wanted. Something else that’s cool about this film is that when they first started, they didn’t really have any idea of what the characters would look like, but as time went on, the animators included things about the actors into the characters! By the end of it, it really seemed as if the characters and the actors were one in the same. Also, we almost didn’t get Lucy Liu in the film! They went back to her three different times, continuing to develop her character until she felt more passionately about playing her. We’ll be getting into all of this and so much more – so make sure to stick around to until the end of the video and leave us a comment telling us who your favorite character is!

snippet.title: The Voices Behind Strange World
snippet.description:
Disney’s Strange World has put together a truly talented voice cast, and we’re taking a look at what it was that made them stand out! Jake Gyllenhaal has been cast as the voice for Searcher Clade, although this isn’t necessarily his first time working with the Walt Disney Company. Jake Gyllenhaal has previously appeared in the Marvel Cinematic Universe playing the villainous Mysterio in Spiderman: Far From Home. Gabrielle Union has been cast to play Searcher’s wife, Meridian Clade. Union has discussed how important she feels that it is for non-traditional families to be represented among the selection on Disney+. Dennis Quaid, who has previously appeared alongside Lindsay Lohan on Disney’s The Parent Trap, takes on a rare voice acting role as Jaeger Clade. Alan Tudyk makes Strange World yet another entry into the growing list of Disney movies he has appeared in. Alan Tudyk has already lent his voice to the role of the droid K-2SO in Star Wars: Rogue One. Alan Tudyk has played the Duke of Weselton in Disney’s Frozen, Pico the Toucan in Encanto, and Tuk Tuk in Raya and the Last Dragon. Outside of his work with Disney, Alan Tudyk also provides the voice for the Joker and Clayface in the HBO animated series Harley Quinn. Lucy Liu has a surprisingly long list of voice acting roles on her resume as well. She has offered her voice for the role of Master Viper in Dreamworks’ Kung Fu Panda series, as well as for the role of Silvermist in Disney’s animated Tinkerbell series.

snippet.title: Behind The Set Of WEDNESDAY
snippet.description:
We have a lot to talk about when it comes to Netflix’s Wednesday series! Not only the fact that Jenna Ortega absolutely slays her role as Wednesday Addams, while still getting to see the OG Addams Family Wednesday, Christina Ricci as Marilyn Thornhill. There are so many incredible things to consider when talking about the set of the show. For one thing, it was filmed in Romania, which is not often utilized in film and TV, but the essence of Bucharest really captures the vibe that Tim Burton and the rest of the team really wanted for the show. There are also tons of easter eggs that reference Tim Burton’s other films. Did you happen to notice anything on the back wall of the Weathervane Cafe? A lot of the set was built at Buftea Studios, the largest and longest film studio in Eastern Europe! They literally do everything from construction to post production. Pilgrim World, the sheriff’s house, the town of Jericho, and the quad were all built there! Speaking of the quad, definitely pay special attention to the gargoyles in that scene. They’re holding some of the show’s big mysteries! Even the arches of the quad were specifically designed to look like demonic faces and things that were linear to the castle’s design! Oh, and don’t worry, we definitely do a deep dive into our favorite appendage, Thing! We cover all of this and more, so make sure to stick around until the end of the video!

snippet.title: 20 Hardest Roles Actors Prepped For
snippet.description:
Being an actor is hard work! These twenty actors know that better than most, considering every single one of them have had days on set they won’t soon forget. Lupita Nyong’o discusses her underwater training for her Black Panther: Wakanda Forever. Penn Badgley talks about his own difficulties in approaching fatherhood alongside Joe from the Netflix series You. Zendaya compared the process of filming one season 2 episode of the HBO series Euphoria to a warzone. Lady Gaga lived as Reggiani for a year and a half while filming Ridley Scott’s House of Gucci. Brendan Fraser struggled with the make-up process for Darren Aronofsky’s The Whale. Marvel Cinematic Universe alumni Tom Holland may have gotten used to doing his own stunts as Spiderman, but he found himself facing an entirely different challenge altogether while filming Uncharted. His co-star from Spiderman: Far From Home, Jake Gyllenhaal, had to adopt a nocturnal lifestyle for the filming of Dan Gilroy’s Nightcrawler. Tom Cruise arranged to use real G-Force while flying the planes for Top Gun: Maverick. Dakota Johnson struggled with her self-confidence after spending a year learning ballet for her role in the 2018 remake to Suspiria. In fact, she panicked so much on set that her co-star Tilda Swinton actually needed to help calm her down! Natalie Portman may have celebrated a heroic return to the Marvel Cinematic Universe with Thor: Love and Thunder, but when she was filming Black Swan she didn’t even know if she was going to survive the project!
